name: us-constitution-amendments

description.en: All 27 amendments to the Constitution of the United States as of 4 October 2026, from the First Amendment (1791) to the Twenty-seventh (1992); the first ten form the Bill of Rights. Front: the amendment, e.g. "Nineteenth Amendment"; back: what it does, summarised in English and Swedish, with the year its ratification was completed in a note. Summaries written from the text of the Constitution as transcribed by the National Archives and printed in the House Manual; numbering and years from Wikidata, the National Archives and the House Manual.
description.sv: Samtliga 27 tillägg till USA:s konstitution per den 4 oktober 2026, från första tillägget (1791) till det tjugosjunde (1992); de tio första utgör Bill of Rights. Framsida: tillägget, t.ex. ”Nittonde tillägget”; baksida: vad det innebär, sammanfattat på engelska och svenska, med året då ratificeringen fullbordades i en anteckning. Sammanfattningarna bygger på konstitutionens text så som National Archives och representanthusets regelsamling (House Manual) återger den; numrering och år från Wikidata, National Archives och House Manual.

method: Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.

1. Wikidata (query 1): every item that is an instance of amendment to the United States Constitution (Q102410240), with its P179 (part of the series) statement for list of amendments to the United States Constitution (Q230698) and that statement's P1545 (series ordinal), its P7588 (effective date) and its English and Swedish labels, was fetched as CSV from the Wikidata Query Service. It returned 27 items with the ordinals 1 to 27 (and the Bill of Rights itself, Q862765, which has no ordinal and was dropped). Query 2 fetched every English, Swedish and mul label and alias of the 27 items. (Query 0 first listed all direct statements of the First Amendment, Q12616, to find the class and properties used.)

2. National Archives (query 4): the transcriptions "The Bill of Rights: A Transcription" (https://www.archives.gov/founding-docs/bill-of-rights-transcript, source nara-bill-of-rights) and "The Constitution: Amendments 11-27" (https://www.archives.gov/founding-docs/amendments-11-27, source nara-amendments-11-27) were downloaded and reduced to plain text with totext.py (scripts and tags removed, one line per paragraph). The first gives the text of Amendments I–X and "These amendments were ratified December 15, 1791"; the second gives, under each of Amendments XI–XXVII, "Passed by Congress … Ratified …" and the text. The Archives list exactly 27 amendments, the last being XXVII ("Originally proposed Sept. 25, 1789. Ratified May 7, 1992.").

3. House Manual (query 5): the Constitution section of the House Manual for the 119th Congress (House Document 118-187, https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/HMAN-119) was downloaded from govinfo as HTML granules, found by trying page numbers: hman.sh fetched pg94 and pg96 to pg132 with the sub-granules pg96-2, pg96-3, pg97-2, pg97-3, pg98-2, pg98-3, pg99-2, pg99-3 and pg99-4. Of these, pg96-3, pg99-4, pg101, pg102, pg105 to pg108, pg115 to pg117, pg121, pg124, pg125, pg128 to pg130 and pg132 returned "Page Not Found", and pg131 is the start of Jefferson's Manual. The amendments are in pg96, pg96-2, pg97, pg97-2, pg97-3, pg98, pg98-2, pg98-3, pg99, pg99-2, pg99-3, pg100, pg103, pg104, pg109 to pg114, pg118, pg119, pg120, pg122, pg123, pg126 and pg127, and Article VII with footnote 1 in pg94; each card's locator names the granules of its section heading and footnote. hman_extract.py joined them into one text and listed each amendment's section headings ("Sec. NNN. …"). The footnote of each amendment states when it was proposed and when "Ratification was completed" (for the Bill of Rights in footnote 1: "Ratification was completed on December 15, 1791."; for the Twenty-first only the proclamation of December 5, 1933).

4. The congress.gov Constitution Annotated (https://constitution.congress.gov/constitution/) and the Senate's Constitution page (https://www.senate.gov/about/origins-foundations/senate-and-constitution/constitution.htm) were tried first as the second official text and both answered 403 to the research environment (query 6); they were not used. A web search for a GPO edition of the amended Constitution led to the House Manual.

5. Cards: one per amendment. Front: the amendment's ordinal name, English "First Amendment" … "Twenty-seventh Amendment" (the ordinal of the Wikidata English label "<Ordinal> Amendment to the United States Constitution", the usual short form) and Swedish "Första tillägget" … "Tjugosjunde tillägget", the pattern of the Wikidata Swedish labels ("Femte tillägget …", "Artonde tillägget …", "Tjugoförsta tillägget …", "Tjugofemte tillägget …") and of the Swedish Wikipedia's list of the amendments, with the Swedish ordinals spelled out; for the First Amendment, whose Wikidata label and Swedish Wikipedia list entry say "Första författningstillägget", the short form "Första tillägget" is confirmed by the Swedish Wikipedia article "Bill of Rights (USA)" and by SVT Nyheter (query 9). Back: what the amendment does, written by the compiler in English and Swedish from the National Archives text and compared with the House Manual's section heading; for amendments that do several things (the Fifth, Sixth, Fourteenth, Twenty-fifth) the back names the main provisions only. The Swedish backs are the compiler's translations of the English public-domain text; for single legal terms the Swedish Wikipedia article was consulted as a guide to established usage (åtalsjury, kapitationsskatt, elektorer, alkoholförbud, skälig misstanke for probable cause, borgenssummor), and one term is used for one concept throughout (due process: rättssäkert förfarande; denying the vote: förvägras). English text follows British spelling ("defence", "summarised") except for words taken from the Constitution itself ("naturalized", "color"). Back note: "Ratified <year>" / "Ratificerat <year>", the year ratification was completed, with "part of the Bill of Rights" on the first ten, the repeal on the Eighteenth and the year of proposal on the Twenty-seventh.

6. Cross-check: make_cards.py read the saved Wikidata CSV, the two National Archives texts, the joined House Manual text and the Swedish Wikipedia wikitext, compared for each amendment the year of Wikidata's P7588, the year of the National Archives' "Ratified" date (1791 for I–X) and the year of the House Manual's "Ratification was completed" (the proclamation year for the Twenty-first); all 27 agree. It then cut each card's evidence verbatim from those texts (a quote is shortened only at a word boundary and marked …; in the National Archives quotes the amendment's heading, e.g. "Amendment I", which stands on its own line on the page, is joined to its text with a colon, and in the House Manual quotes GPO typesetting codes are printed as the characters they stand for, e.g. "Women<n-iden-2>s" as "Women's" and "Citizenship<ls-thn-eq> security" as "Citizenship: security" (the colon read from the printed page, granule HMAN-119-pg104 as PDF, query 10); the quotes for the Sixth and Fourteenth Amendments were extended in quality-control round 1 to show the whole clauses the backs summarise) and wrote cards.json, from which make_dossier.py wrote this dossier; the card texts (fronts, backs, notes) are fixed strings in make_cards.py. The day-level differences between sources, which do not affect any card, are recorded under Quality control. The scripts are not published with the deck; the rules above are what they do.

7. Swedish: the Swedish article "USA:s konstitution" was fetched with its revision id through the MediaWiki API (query 3); its section "Tillägg" lists every amendment as "''<Ordningstal> tillägget'' (<år>)", which was compared with each Swedish front. The Swedish Wikipedia was used for verification only.

8. Recency: no amendment has been added since 1992. On 4 October 2026 the National Archives page and the House Manual of the 119th Congress list 27 amendments. The Equal Rights Amendment, which some call the 28th Amendment, has not been certified or published as part of the Constitution: in its "Statement on the Equal Rights Amendment Ratification Process" of December 17, 2024 (https://www.archives.gov/press/press-releases/2025/nr25-004, query 7) the Archivist and Deputy Archivist said that "the Equal Rights Amendment (ERA) cannot be certified as part of the Constitution due to established legal, judicial, and procedural decisions" and that "the Archivist of the United States cannot legally publish the Equal Rights Amendment"; a web search (query 7) found reports from January 2025 that President Biden had declared it ratified, contradicting the Archivist, and nothing that has changed its status since. It is not in this deck. The Supreme Court's decision in Trump v. Barbara (30 June 2026), found by a web search (query 7), interpreted the Fourteenth Amendment's citizenship clause ("subject to the jurisdiction thereof"); it did not change the amendment's text, which the card summarises.

9. Machine checks: for every card the builder checks against live Wikidata that the item is an amendment to the United States Constitution (P31 Q102410240), that its English label is "<Ordinal> Amendment to the United States Constitution" (which ties the item to the number on the front) and that the year of its P7588 is the year in the back note. The summaries on the backs are not machine-checkable; they rest on the National Archives text and the House Manual headings recorded in each card's evidence. The built deck was validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (validate_sources.ts).
selection: All 27 amendments to the Constitution of the United States, as of 4 October 2026: the ten of the Bill of Rights (ratified 1791) and the seventeen later ones (1795–1992), the set listed by the National Archives and the House Manual and returned by Wikidata. Repealed amendments are included (the Eighteenth, repealed by the Twenty-first). Left out: amendments proposed by Congress but never ratified (among them the first of the twelve articles of 1789, the Titles of Nobility, Corwin and Child Labor amendments and the District of Columbia Voting Rights Amendment), and the Equal Rights Amendment, which some call the 28th Amendment but which the National Archives has not certified (method step 8); and the articles of the original Constitution. Each back summarises the amendment's main effect; the many details of the longer amendments (the Fourteenth's sections 2–5, the Twentieth's sections 3–6, the Twenty-fifth's procedure) are left out to keep the cards short.

Where a Swedish back resembles the article's summary (the Seventeenth, Twenty-first, Twenty-second, Twenty-fourth), both are close translations of the same short English sentence; the Tenth's back was reworded in quality-control round 1 so that it does not follow the article's translation. SVT Nyheter (all rights reserved) was consulted for one Swedish name only; nothing was copied. The selection is the complete set of 27 amendments, which every list shares.

findings.issue: The Swedish back renders "probable cause" as "skälig misstanke", the lower of the two Swedish grades of suspicion; the reviewer suggested the higher grade, "sannolika skäl", as the usual Swedish rendering of the US standard.
findings.resolution: Declined. No source was found that renders the US "probable cause" as "sannolika skäl", and the reviewer cited none. The Swedish Wikipedia sources checked today (query 11) use the lower grade or a neutral phrase: "USA:s konstitution" (revision 59500995) says the Fourth Amendment "förbjuder arrestering och husrannsakan annat än på skälig misstanke med särskilt beslut", and the translation in "Bill of Rights (USA)" (revision 59500249) has "utom uppå skälig grund". "Misstankegrad" (revision 59250090) notes that in Swedish law a search (husrannsakan) can be carried out at the grade "skäligen misstänkt", so "skälig misstanke" is the Swedish threshold for the very measure the card is about, while "på sannolika skäl misstänkt" is the grade tied to arrest and detention. A US standard maps onto neither Swedish grade exactly; the card keeps the term documented in method step 5.
